cohort: 42,950 singleton, cephalic, first births following uncomplicated pregnancies at 37-40 completed weeks' gestation ('standard primiparae') in Victoria, Australia, from 2000-2005
finding: Induction of labor in medically uncomplicated nulliparous women at term carries a more than doubling of risk of emergency CS, compared with spontaneous labor, with no impact on perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: All methods of induction and augmentation of labor were associated with an increase in the rate of CS.
